prospect.name: Daniel Borunda
prospect.occupation: Owner of a solar maintenance business, in its tenth year, with two employees; works on site himself, on roofs and ladders, as well as quoting, selling and inspecting. Currently two weeks into a $6,000 AI automation course with the intention of starting an AI agency.
prospect.family_status: Married; wife works at a hospital on an unpredictable schedule. Three children - one aged 18 and two young.
prospect.training_background: Wrestled in high school at 130-135 lb; six years military, leaving around 160 lb. Two years of heavy keto from around age 34 took him to 160-170. Deliberately bulked to 185 with hypertrophy and heavy time-under-tension work for bone density. Trains at a commercial gym at 4-4:30am, bodybuilding style, in nine-to-twelve-month blocks with year-long gaps. Uses intermittent fasting, one-meal-a-day and multi-day fasting; owns a self-built automated cold tub, a sauna, a flow rope, two kettlebells (7 lb and 15 lb), 70 lb adjustable Powerblocks and a weight bench, plus a $100/month gym membership.
prospect.medical: No conditions, injuries or medications were disclosed, and none were asked for. On day three of an extended water fast at the time of the call, taking only electrolyte water, and understood by the rep to be aiming for seven to ten days. Self-experiments with supplementation including peptides, NMN and NR - 'my own guinea pig type of thing with research... some things are newer in research and I test them out.' Reports joints and connective tissue having tightened up with the extra weight. His father had a long terminal illness that reached its end around two years ago; the nature of the illness was never asked and no hereditary risk question was put.

signals: Lost ground to a hard season, named precisely: 'my dad got sick... for those two years, you know, just going and seeing them at the hospital, checking in on them... I just kind of stopped focusing on myself, my exercise and all that. So I kind of ballooned up.'
Wants a former self back and has a number for it - 185 down to 180, from a current 200-206 and a peak of 211
Carries the regret openly: 'then I have no idea why I stopped, but I really don't'

Strong secondary reading is skeptical_bargain_hunter, and it is the reading that explains the outcome: he is self-directed and capable, his own cheap methods genuinely worked (keto took him to 160, three days of fasting took six pounds off during the call), and he is anchored to $129-$199 a month one-to-one coaching
Also carries optimizer surface features - cold plunge, sauna, peptides, mouth taping, sleep hacking - but he is 25 lb above his own target, which is rebuilding rather than good-to-great

goals.text: Have access to enough energy for what he calls three days in one day - morning, work day and evening with the family
Lose about 20-25 lb of fat, from 200-206 down to 180, keeping the roughly 10 lb of muscle he built
Always be able to say yes when his two small children ask to get on his shoulders
Acquire as many science-backed tools for losing weight as he already has for gaining it
Loosen joints and connective tissue that have tightened up with the added weight
Be able to train the same way while travelling, which he identifies as where his consistency breaks

pains.text: Energy is unreliable and cascades - a heavy day on the roof knocks down the evening and the following morning
Eats junk - sweets, cookies, pancakes, chips - at least once a day, which he identifies as the whole 25 lb gain
Stopped training entirely for two years while his father was terminally ill and has never fully explained to himself why he stopped
Trains in nine-to-twelve-month blocks separated by year-long gaps
Believes he lacks tools for losing weight while having many for gaining it
Extremely time-poor - runs a two-employee business hands-on, has three children, and is doing a full-time AI course nine to five on top
Joints and connective tissue tightened up carrying the extra weight
Has accepted internally that it may take another full year to come back down

objections.raw_quote: Oh, that's definitely more than I thought it was going to be.
objections.rep_response: Isolated it correctly and got confirmation that the only blocker was money, then asked what he had available. But offered no payment plan at all; instead disclosed two cheaper products in sequence - a $3,000 six-month version and Primal University at $199/month or $1,000 for six months.

objections.raw_quote: I paid $6,000 for an AI automation course. So I'm doing that now... So that's way out of the realistic, what I'm able to do and willing to do
objections.rep_response: Accepted it without challenge and wished him well on the course - 'Well, I hope that's going to work very well for you'. No exploration of cash, monthly surplus, credit or assets, and no attempt to structure the amount over time.

objections.raw_quote: One-on-one trainings, coaching programs are around $129 to $199 a month. So that's what I kind of thought you guys were at.
objections.rep_response: Positioned Trevor as the biggest name in the kettlebell space and stated that genuine one-to-one in the space runs $3,000-$4,000 for six months, then offered to research the competitor himself and told the prospect to buy the competitor if it turned out to be real one-to-one at that price.

evidence: No decision either way and the conversation was explicitly left running: 'let's stay in contact... I'll follow up with you in a couple of days too'
Counter-evidence, and it is strong: the prospect ranked Primal below at least one and possibly two competitors - 'I'd probably put you guys, you know, second or third'
He intends to speak to a YouTube coach he trusts first, and to finish his fast before comparing
No payment, no meeting booked, no commitment of any kind
The rep undercut his own follow-up by offering to vet the competitor and telling him to buy them if the price held up: 'if that's literally one-on-one coaching for that amount, I would say do it'
outcome.next_step: Prospect to identify the competing YouTube coach and send the name to the rep, who will assess it for him; rep to follow up in a few days

notable.note: Three things. First, two undisclosed price points surfaced under pressure - a $3,000 six-month 'different version' and Primal University at $199/month or $1,000 for six months - neither of which is in the audited structure, and the $3,000 tier was not offered to a prospect on this same rep's earlier call who could not afford $6,000 and was instead sold an interest-bearing instalment plan totalling $7,200. Second, no payment plan was offered here at all; price was cut instead. Third, the rep behaved unusually honestly at the end, offering to research the competitor and advising the prospect to buy them if their one-to-one claim held up - commercially costly but worth knowing. The setter is named on the call as Derek, which may be the identity behind the DH suffix seen elsewhere in the corpus, though this file carries no suffix.
